title: Flash Boys
author: Michael Lewis
notes: Fun read. Provides interesting insights into the world of High Frequency Trading

title: Origin
author: Dan Brown
notes: Interesting read. The main thing I didn't like is that a cliff-hanger spans almost the whole book. I had to spoil it for myself after enough teasing of the big reveal.

title: The Da Vinci Code
author: Dan Brown
notes: Interesting read. Provocative from a religious standpoint.

title: Inferno
author: Dan Brown
notes: The first Robert Langdon book, and in my opinion, the best one.

title: The Art of War
author: Sun Tzu
notes: I had been looking forward to this one but ultimately found it underwhelming. It it just a collection of insights about armed conflict.

title: Ghost Wars
author: Steve Coll
notes: Interesting content, but tough read. It details CIA activities in the Middle East that preceded and motivated the 9/11 attack.

title: The Screwtape Letters
author: C.S. Lewis
notes: A creative idea: a senior demon writing letters to instruct his nephew on how to lead a human into temptation. It was recommended to me, but I found it just okay.

title: Outliers
author: Malcolm Gladwell
notes: Intriguing read. Sensible explanation for the why some individuals among us are outliers.

title: The Running Man
author: Stephen King
notes: Sort of a fun story, but not a favorite. Book was about the same caliber as the movie that was eventually made, 6.4/10 on IMDB.

title: Never Split the Difference
author: Chris Voss
notes: Interesting read by a former FBI hostage negotiator.

title: Holly
author: Stephen King
notes: I had high hopes for this one when I heard it was in development. Ultimately I was underwhelmed

title: The Long Walk
author: Stephen King
notes: Pretty entertaining read. The movie wasn't bad either, better than its 6.7/10 IMDB rating. Oddly, the movie significantly altered the ending, perhaps to make it more cinematic.

title: Dolores Claiborne
author: Stephen King
notes: Entertaining and a unique style. The story is told as a continuous, breathless, unedited, first-person monologue.
